findings.body: Removing `@require_role("admin")` leaves `DELETE /users/<user>` with no authorization check. Any unauthenticated caller can now delete any name in `USERS` and receive 204. Grant cleanup jobs an admin or dedicated service role (or a separate authenticated internal route) instead of dropping the decorator.

summary:
Looks good is the wrong verdict here: this PR removes the only authorization check on `DELETE /users/<user>`, so any caller can delete accounts. Cleanup jobs that 403'd as `viewer` need an admin or service identity, not an open delete endpoint.

`app.py` is the entire surface. After this change `require_role` is unused, there is no `before_request` or other gate, and `delete_user` still mutates the in-memory `USERS` list and returns 204. That is a broken-authorization regression on a destructive route.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch removes `@require_role("admin")` from `DELETE /users/<user>`, and the head handler only calls `USERS.remove(user)` with no auth check, so any caller can delete entries and get 204. Base still had the decorator on that route.
